## Glossary

**Cascade resolution**  
Owner-tier walk that picks the winning row: user chain (SpaceUser → OrganizationUser → User → default) or org chain (Space → Organization → default).

**{{#component:slug}}**  
Inline block markup that marks a reusable component inside authored MJML.

**componentRefs**  
Pre-computed, slug-keyed list of components an MJML body references; resolved through the cascade at read time, never stored as ids.

**componentVersions**  
AuditLog map of slug → child snapshot id stamped by the emailVersioning hook, forming the version tree.

**composeTemplate**  
Phase 1 of render: resolve a template by slug through the cascade and expand its components; returns the winning owner.

**{{#each}}**  
Loop block over a collection; rules inside it are rewritten into array rules by scopedRule.

**email-templates**  
Class tag: email templates and components, MJML, component refs, cascade, render/save, the email lens and rule blocks.

**EmailComponent**  
Prisma model for a reusable MJML fragment (header, footer, button) referenced by slug from templates or other components.

**EmailLens**  
Four lenses, one per scope root, that decide which tokens, paths and rules a template may use.

**emailLensFor**  
API builder of a slug's owner-scoped email lens from the registry entry, DEFAULT_RECIPIENT_NARROWING and the row's stored slots.

**EmailOwnerModel**  
Owner discriminator for email rows: default, admin, Organization, Space, and the user tiers User, OrganizationUser, SpaceUser.

**EmailTemplate**  
Prisma model for a whole sendable MJML message with slug, locale, subject, kind, componentRefs and owner.

**emailTemplateAuditLogId**  
CommunicationLog column pinning the template snapshot that was sent, used by recompose.

**{{#if rule=…}}**  
Conditional block whose json-rules condition is checked at save and evaluated through the lens at render.

**inheritToSpaces**  
Flag letting a Space resolve its Organization's template or component in the cascade.

**interpolate**  
Phase 2 of render, per recipient: evaluate conditions and substitute tokens, narrowed to the lens, reporting issues to a sink.

**mapRefs**  
Extracts component blocks from MJML, deduplicating identical variants and indexing different ones (:0, :1).

**onIssue**  
Registry render policy: platform (stable unbranded fallback), fail (retry/DLQ), or degrade (send with empty blocks).

**OPAQUE_SLOT**  
The opaque data bag, addressable at any depth; a loop over it may not read lens-backed roots (opaqueLoopIssue).

**Preflight**  
Pre-send checks on a template (subject present, images have alt, preheader, spam phrases, unresolved lens paths) via runPreflight / emailTemplatePreflight.

**recomposeSnapshot**  
Rebuilds the as-sent composition by splicing pinned component snapshots back into the template snapshot.

**registry**  
apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts: per-slug entry declaring entity lenses, slots and render policy.

**RenderIssue**  
Typed render-time issue (kind rule | token | each, path, detail) emitted instead of throwing.

**Rule reference**  
A RuleReference edge from an email template or component to a row its rule names (tag, organization, space, segment), synced on save.

**RuleErrorSink**  
Callback (issue: RenderIssue) => void that collects render issues for degraded rules, failed filters and empty tokens.

**Scope roots**  
The four token roots a template may read: sender, recipient, data, system (SCOPE_ROOTS).

**settleTemplate**  
API entry that resolves a template through the cascade and renders subject and body with system tokens and RenderIssue collection.

**substitute**  
Registry option naming an alternate template to send on render issues; substitutes cannot chain.

**System tokens**  
Platform-provided {{system.*}} values such as the unsubscribe URL; sender-specific values use {{sender.*}}.

**withRule**  
The one fork through which a stored rule is evaluated: degraded (issue, never a match) or sound (run the evaluator).

## 1. What this Warden covers

How an email's content is stored, validated, resolved and rendered in the template: owner-scoped MJML templates and reusable components, the cascade that picks which row wins, the four-root email lens that governs tokens and rules, the save pipeline that validates and records rule references, and the two-phase compose/interpolate render.

## 2. The domain

Email content lives in two models, `EmailTemplate` (a whole sendable message with subject and `kind`) and `EmailComponent` (a reusable MJML fragment marked inline as `{{#component:slug}}…{{/component:slug}}`). Both are owned through false polymorphism (`ownerModel`: default, admin, User, Organization, Space, OrganizationUser, SpaceUser) and resolved through a cascade chosen by the sender's tier: a user actor walks SpaceUser → OrganizationUser → User → default, a tenant sender walks Space → Organization (only with `inheritToSpaces`) → default. Component refs stay slug-keyed and late-bound through that cascade, so an override takes effect without re-saving. `composeTemplate` / `composeComponent` (built on `lookupCascade`, `cascadeLookups`, `firstResolved`, `ownerWhere`, `expand`) do the lookup; never hand-write tier loops.

Writing goes through one door: `saveEmailTemplate` (the api wrapper, also used by seeds through `emailSeedSavers`) and `saveEmailComponents`. Save validates MJML (`validateMjml`), conditions (`assertValidConditions` / `validateConditions`), tokens (`validateTokens`), reference cycles (`validateNoCycle`) and same-owner dependents (`validateDependents`) against the composed template, then syncs `RuleReference` edges (`syncRuleReferences`). Rendering is two-phase: compose once per template, then interpolate per recipient (`settleTemplate`, `renderForRecipient` / `recipientVariables`, `interpolate`, `evaluateConditions`). Render never throws on drift: degraded rules and bad tokens render empty and become `RenderIssue`s in a `RuleErrorSink`, and the email `registry` entry's render policy (`fail` / `degrade` / `substitute`, `onIssue`) decides the send; subject issues are always fatal. The email lens (`emailLens`, four lenses for `sender`, `recipient`, `data`, `system`) is the single vocabulary for tokens and rules at save, render, preflight and in the builder (`emailSurface`), scoped to the row owner and the sender (`scopeEmailLens`, `senderLensOwner`), and `narrowVariables` enforces its projection on the variables at render. Versioning is in the audit log (`AuditLog.componentVersions`), so `recomposeCommunication` / `recomposeSnapshot` rebuild what was sent.

Not here: the send pipeline itself (`sendEmail` planner, `deliverEmail`, `CommunicationLog` statuses, providers, preferences, contacts) is the delivery-messaging-contacts region; the json-rules engine, generic lenses (`lensFor`, `clampLens`, `walkLensPath` in json-rules) and the general `RuleReference` / `withRule` / `syncRuleReferenceEdges` machinery belong to json-rules; segments themselves are customers-segments. This region owns their email-shaped fronts.

### Class `email-templates`: Email templates and components: MJML, component refs, cascade, render/save, the email lens and rule blocks

- **EmailComponent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/emailComponent.prisma`: Shared partials referenced via componentRefs; full sendable messages with subject: EmailTemplate instead.
- **EmailTemplate** `packages/db/prisma/schema/emailTemplate.prisma`: Whole messages with subject and kind; reusable fragments belong in EmailComponent.
- **applyEmailLens** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#applyEmailLens`: For evaluating a rule; emailRuleReferences only lists the rows it names, emailRuleViolations only validates it.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* calling json-rules check(rule, data) directly on a stored email rule without rewriting it through the lens (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § The email lens (settle never checks a raw rule))
- **assertValidConditions** `packages/email/src/validations/validateConditions/assertValidConditions.ts#assertValidConditions`: fail fast on email content conditions whose rule paths the lens cannot resolve
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* saving template MJML/subject without checking {{#if rule=…}} paths against the lens, leaving the error to surface at render (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Save Pipeline (fail fast instead of shipping a render-time time-bomb))
- **assertValidTokens** `packages/email/src/validations/validateTokens/assertValidTokens.ts#assertValidTokens`: Throws on token issues; validateConditions returns condition issues instead of throwing.
- **canNestMjml** `packages/email/src/render/authoring.ts#canNestMjml`: prefer over reading MJML_CHILD_TAGS directly
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* reading MJML_CHILD_TAGS directly, or a hand-written table of which mj-* tags may contain which (catalog: canNestMjml (prefer over reading MJML_CHILD_TAGS directly))
- **canNestMjml** `packages/email/src/render/mjmlNesting.ts#canNestMjml`: Prefer over reading MJML_CHILD_TAGS directly; treats a null parent as root, so anything nests.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* reading MJML_CHILD_TAGS directly, or a hand-written table of which mj-* tags may contain which (catalog: canNestMjml (prefer over reading MJML_CHILD_TAGS directly))
- **cascadeLookups** `packages/email/src/render/owner.ts#cascadeLookups`: Pair with firstResolved for owner fallback; use ownerCascade alone when only the tier list is needed.
- **checkExpectations** `packages/email/src/rules/componentExpectations.ts#checkExpectations`: Need per-path pass/fail; for warning strings only use collectUnprovidedPathWarnings.
- **collectComponentRegions** `packages/email/src/render/authoring.ts#collectComponentRegions`: already-parsed nodes: collectComponentRegionsFromNodes instead
- **collectComponentRegions** `packages/email/src/render/regions.ts#collectComponentRegions`: From an MJML string; with already parsed nodes use collectComponentRegionsFromNodes.
- **collectHydrationPaths** `packages/email/src/rules/collectHydrationPaths.ts#collectHydrationPaths`: Need all path kinds; collectConditionFieldPaths for field paths alone.
- **collectJsonOpacityWarnings** `packages/email/src/rules/collectJsonOpacityWarnings.ts#collectJsonOpacityWarnings`: For paths absent from the lens entirely: collectUnprovidedPathWarnings instead.
- **collectRules** `packages/email/src/render/conditionParser/collectRules.ts#collectRules`: Use to check email conditions against a lens; skips rules on loop indexes, elements or other lens roots.
- **collectSlugs** `packages/email/src/render/decompose.ts#collectSlugs`: list the component slugs used in an MJML email template
- **collectSlugsFromNodes** `packages/email/src/render/nodes.ts#collectSlugsFromNodes`: gather the unique slugs referenced across an email node tree
- **collectUnprovidedPathWarnings** `packages/email/src/rules/componentExpectations.ts#collectUnprovidedPathWarnings`: Paths under JSON fields: collectJsonOpacityWarnings; structured per-path results: checkExpectations.
- **composeComponent** `packages/email/src/render/compose.ts#composeComponent`: Single reusable component only; for a full email with its referenced components use composeTemplate.
- **composeTemplate** `packages/email/src/render/compose.ts#composeTemplate`: Use for whole emails; composeComponent for one component. Returns owner — the row that won the cascade — for settling sender.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written loop of prisma.emailTemplate.findFirst calls per ownerModel (Space, then Organization, then default) followed by string-replacing {{#component:…}} blocks (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Email › Cascade Resolution (the cascade happens automatically during compose))
- **computeDegradedComponentRefs** `packages/email/src/render/computeDegradedComponentRefs.ts#computeDegradedComponentRefs`: list component slugs referenced in MJML that lookup cannot resolve
- **contentDynamicRuleReferences** `packages/email/src/rules/ruleReferences.ts#contentDynamicRuleReferences`: extract dynamic rule references from email content strings using the lens
- **contentReferenceScopes** `packages/email/src/rules/ruleReferences.ts#contentReferenceScopes`: need references split by slot lens; flat list: contentRuleReferences instead
- **contentRuleReferences** `packages/email/src/rules/ruleReferences.ts#contentRuleReferences`: flat reference list; per-slot scopes: contentReferenceScopes instead
- **decompose** `packages/email/src/render/authoring.ts#decompose`: Use with parseBlocks for component extraction; decomposeNodes is its lower-level node pass.
- **decompose** `packages/email/src/render/decompose.ts#decompose`: Use on raw MJML strings; decomposeNodes when you already hold parsed nodes.
- **DEFAULT_RECIPIENT_NARROWING** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#DEFAULT_RECIPIENT_NARROWING`: default recipient fields and tag relations exposed to email templates
- **defaultEmailLens** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#defaultEmailLens`: When no sender/data context exists; build one with emailLens when you have a sender or data.
- **deriveComponentExpectations** `packages/email/src/rules/componentExpectations.ts#deriveComponentExpectations`: Produces the expectations list that checkExpectations then validates against a lens.
- **deriveTextFromHtml** `packages/email/src/render/deriveTextFromHtml.ts#deriveTextFromHtml`: produce plain-text email body from rendered HTML with collapsed whitespace
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-rolled tag-stripping regex to build the plain-text part of an email (catalog: deriveTextFromHtml (produce plain-text email body from rendered HTML))
- **emailLens** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#emailLens`: When you have sender or data context; defaultEmailLens otherwise.
- **EmailRenderError** `packages/email/src/errors/EmailRenderError.ts#EmailRenderError`: Render-time failures; provider send failures: EmailProviderError; invalid rules: ConditionValidationError.
- **emailRuleDecoration** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#emailRuleDecoration`: derive one rule-editor facet per scope root present in the email lens
- **emailRuleReferences** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#emailRuleReferences`: For named rows; emailDynamicRuleReferences for runtime-resolved refs, applyEmailLens to evaluate.
- **emailRuleViolations** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#emailRuleViolations`: To get issues directly; emailRuleVocabulary when a RuleVocabulary object must be passed in.
- **emailSurface** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#emailSurface`: Rule builder UI only; save and settle paths keep the full EmailLens instead.
- **emailTemplatePreflight** `apps/api/src/modules/emailTemplate/services/emailTemplatePreflight.ts#emailTemplatePreflight`: Validate a template before send; to inspect what rule data a template can reference, use emailTemplateRuleSurface instead.
- **emailTemplateRuleSurface** `apps/api/src/modules/emailTemplate/services/emailTemplateRuleSurface.ts#emailTemplateRuleSurface`: Use to feed rule editors with available template data; for validating a template's content use emailTemplatePreflight.
- **emailTokenPathKind** `packages/email/src/validations/validateTokens/tokenPathKind.ts#emailTokenPathKind`: Email lenses: use this; generic Lens or LensNarrowing: tokenPathKind instead.
- **evaluateConditions** `packages/email/src/render/evaluateConditions.ts#evaluateConditions`: Runtime branch evaluation; guardedToken only writes an exists-guarded token into templates.
- **evaluateScopedRule** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#evaluateScopedRule`: Inside loops over a collection element; whole-message rules use the general rule evaluator.
- **expand** `packages/email/src/render/expand.ts#expand`: Default for owner-scoped lookup; expandWith to supply a custom component lookup (tests, previews).
- **expandWith** `packages/email/src/render/expand.ts#expandWith`: Custom lookup only; normal rendering uses expand.
- **firstResolved** `packages/email/src/render/owner.ts#firstResolved`: Runs lookups sequentially and stops at the first hit; usually fed by cascadeLookups.
- **guardedToken** `packages/email/src/render/guardedToken.ts#guardedToken`: Writing template text; evaluateConditions resolves it at render.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-writing an exists {{#if …}} wrapper with fallback text around a token (catalog: guardedToken (emit a variable token wrapped in an exists-condition with fallback text))
- **hydrate** `packages/email/src/render/hydrate.ts#hydrate`: Custom body resolver; hydrateCascade for owner-scoped cascade lookup. Not the Prisma relation hydrate in FEATURES.md.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* deep hand-written `include: { a: { include: { b: ... } } }` trees or per-row relation fetch loops (N+1), instead of `hydrate(accessor, record)` (FEATURES.md § Hydration System)
- **hydrateCascade** `packages/email/src/render/hydrate.ts#hydrateCascade`: Default for stored templates; hydrate when supplying your own body resolver.
- **interpolate** `packages/email/src/render/interpolate.ts#interpolate`: fill template placeholders with variables, narrowed to the lens projection, reporting errors to a sink
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* String.replace / regex substitution of {{sender.*}}, {{recipient.*}} or {{data.*}} placeholders, or calling substituteVariables directly (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Variable Interpolation and § Render Pipeline; catalog: substituteVariables (use via interpolate))
- **isRailProvidedSystemField** `packages/email/src/rules/railProvidedSystemFields.ts#isRailProvidedSystemField`: Prefer over checking RAIL_PROVIDED_SYSTEM_FIELDS directly; narrows the type.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* checking RAIL_PROVIDED_SYSTEM_FIELDS.includes(field) or a hard-coded list of rail-filled system fields (catalog: isRailProvidedSystemField (prefer over checking RAIL_PROVIDED_SYSTEM_FIELDS directly))
- **isStructurallyBalanced** `packages/email/src/render/conditionParser/isStructurallyBalanced.ts#isStructurallyBalanced`: check that if/each condition blocks in template text open and close in balanced order
- **isValidBindingIdentifier** `packages/email/src/render/conditionParser/grammar.ts#isValidBindingIdentifier`: Also reject reserved names: combine with RESERVED_BINDING_NAMES.
- **lensPathFields** `packages/email/src/rules/walkLensPath.ts#lensPathFields`: Only need field entries; for the full walk result use walkLensPath.
- **lookupCascade** `packages/email/src/render/lookupCascade.ts#lookupCascade`: Several components at once; lookupComponent for one slug, lookupAtOwner for a single tier.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* calling lookupComponent or findFirst once per slug in a loop to resolve many components (catalog: lookupCascade (several components at once))
- **lookupComponent** `packages/email/src/render/lookupTemplate.ts#lookupComponent`: One slug; for many slugs use lookupCascade.
- **lookupLens** `packages/email/src/render/lookupTemplate.ts#lookupLens`: Only have a slug; if the template row is already loaded use templateLens.
- **lookupTemplate** `packages/email/src/render/lookupTemplate.ts#lookupTemplate`: Full template row; lookupLens when only the lens is needed, lookupAtOwner for one tier.
- **narrowToElements** `packages/email/src/rules/scopedRule.ts#narrowToElements`: evaluating at render with a concrete element; rewriting the rule itself: scopedRule instead

- **parseBlocks** `packages/email/src/render/authoring.ts#parseBlocks`: Entry point for parsing; pair with decompose for component extraction, serialize to write back.
- **parseBlocks** `packages/email/src/render/parseBlocks.ts#parseBlocks`: Raw node tree; for component regions only use collectComponentRegions instead.
- **recipientVariables** `apps/api/src/lib/email/renderForRecipient.ts#recipientVariables`: Build variables here, then interpolate with renderForRecipient.

- **saveEmailTemplate** `packages/email/src/render/save.ts#saveEmailTemplate`: Canonical template save path; saveTemplate is the raw row write without checks or reference sync.

- **SCOPE_ROOTS** `packages/email/src/render/conditionParser/grammar.ts#SCOPE_ROOTS`: Membership checks: RESERVED_SCOPE_ROOTS instead.

- **useEmailRuleSurface** `packages/ui/src/hooks/email/useEmailRuleSurface.ts#useEmailRuleSurface`: Template rule surface: this; variables in scope for a rule source: useEmailVariableScope instead.

- **validateConditions** `packages/email/src/validations/validateConditions/validateConditions.ts#validateConditions`: Template condition/loop checks; tokens: assertValidTokens; MJML markup: validateMjml; partial reference cycles: validateNoCycle.
- **validateDependents** `packages/email/src/render/validateDependents.ts#validateDependents`: Same-owner checks only; other owners' templates are handled by the versioning hook.

- **validateTokens** `packages/email/src/validations/validateTokens/validateTokens.ts#validateTokens`: Whole-template validation; use emailTokenPathKind or unknownMustaches only for single-path or stray-brace checks.
- **visibleText** `packages/email/src/preflight/visibleText.ts#visibleText`: extract user-visible text from email HTML
- **walkConditionTree** `packages/email/src/rules/walkConditionTree.ts#walkConditionTree`: visit every node of a rule condition tree with a caller context
- **walkEmailLensPath** `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts#walkEmailLensPath`: Walking email template token paths; use resolveBindingPath for rewriting paths through binding chains.
- **walkLensPath** `packages/email/src/rules/walkLensPath.ts#walkLensPath`: Full walk result; just field entries: lensPathFields.
- **apps/api/src/modules/emailTemplate** `apps/api/src/modules/emailTemplate`: preflight email templates and expose their rule surface to superadmins
- **Adding a referenceable model** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md`: make a model referenceable by rules
- **CAS claim queued→sending** `lib/email/deliverEmailMessage.ts`: Per-row at-most-once claims; cross-process critical sections use locks instead.
- **CommunicationLog find-or-create** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Planner (sendEmail)`: dedupe per-recipient sends via queued log row keyed on idempotencyKey
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* relying on BullMQ job ids or an in-memory set to avoid duplicate sends, or creating a fresh log row per attempt (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Planner (sendEmail) step 3 (the at-most-once fence, durable beyond BullMQ retention))
- **component block markup** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Communications`: mark reusable email components inline in MJML templates
- **Edge staleness via soft delete and purge** `ruleReference:target`: copy target soft deletes onto edges; purge nulls FK keeping targetId
- **Email ownership cascade** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Email > Database Models`: resolve templates by ownerModel false polymorphism with Space→Org→default and user chains
- **Email planner/deliver fan-out** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Send Pipeline`: plan email once, then deliver per recipient as separate queued jobs
- **Email slow lane for wide fan-outs** `JOBS.md § Fast and Slow Lanes`: Large sends: slow lane; small sends stay on the fast lane.
- **Referenced model path source** `docs: email lens sources`: point a referenced model's path source at its own model source
- **Shutdown-aware backoff** `lib/email/deliverEmailMessage.ts`: Retry loops held inside a claim that must not strand rows on deploy.
- **Template and component cascade resolution** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Cascade Resolution`: User-actor senders walk user chain; tenant/shared senders walk org chain; Space inherits Org only with inheritToSpaces.
- **Template versioning via audit log** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#template-versioning--recompose`: Reconstructing what was sent; never pin versions on live EmailTemplate/EmailComponent rows.
- **Two-phase email render pipeline** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Render Pipeline`: compose template once, then interpolate per recipient
- **admitRuleReferences** `packages/db`: refuse new references the lens source's composed where does not admit
- **AuditLog.componentVersions** `AuditLog`: map child slugs to snapshot audit-log ids, forming a traversable version tree
- **bindOptional** `@template/shared/rules`: mark a rule binding that may be omitted and resolve to null
- **canDeliver** `Email docs § Deliver gate ②`: Preference gate after inScope; deliverability is a separate bouncer check.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* inline checks like contact.acceptedKinds.includes(kind) or kind === 'system' before a send (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Communication Preferences and § Messaging (the shared gate for both lanes))
- **clampLens** `json-rules`: bound a lens slot's narrowing with an extra filter
- **CommunicationChannel** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Database Models > Enums`: select delivery channel email, sms, push or inApp
- **CommunicationKind** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Database Models > Enums`: system always delivers; platform/activity opt-out; marketing opt-in only
- **CommunicationLog** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Database Models > CommunicationLog`: record one delivery row per recipient per send, deduplicated by idempotencyKey
- **CommunicationLog.renderIssues** `CommunicationLog`: record render issues of a degraded send for later inspection
- **CommunicationStatus** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Database Models > Enums`: track delivery state queued→sending→sent or failed/suppressed/undeliverable
- **composeNarrowed** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > The email lens`: build the narrowed lens the builder gates against
- **Contact.deliverability** `Email docs § Deliverability`: cache bouncer pre-flight result for 30 days to skip undeliverable addresses
- **createConsoleClient** `packages/email/src/client/console.ts`: local development; createResendClient for real delivery
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an if (NODE_ENV !== 'production') branch that skips or fakes the send (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Email Clients)
- **createResendClient** `packages/email/src/client/resend.ts`: production delivery; createConsoleClient in development
- **db.findForUpdate** `packages/db`: row-level locks within a txn; cross-process work uses createLock
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a raw $queryRaw `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, or a read-then-update in a transaction with no row lock (docs/claude/DATABASE.md § Row Locks and Create-If-Missing)
- **deliverEmail** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Planner (sendEmail)`: re-read recipient at send time, resolve cc/bcc, send and log
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* enqueueJob('deliverEmail', …) from anywhere but the planner (catalog: deliverEmail (enqueued by sendEmail; do not enqueue 'deliverEmail' directly))
- **describeRuleSources** `json-rules >= 3.0`: low-level; prefer ruleReferences which interprets id sources via the registry
- **dynamicRuleReferences** `packages/db`: flag rule leaves whose referenced rows cannot be checked at save
- **EMAIL_SLOW_LANE_MIN_RECIPIENTS** `Email docs § Dispatch`: set the recipient count above which email fan-out runs on the slow lane
- **EmailClient.send** `packages/email/src/client/types.ts`: deliver one email with recipients, sender, subject, HTML, tags and metadata
- **EmailEntry** `apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts`: declare per-template entity, sender, recipients, cc/bcc and data as lenses
- **emailLensFor** `apps/api/src/lib/email/emailLensFor.ts`: Use for any email save, edit, render or send lens; never hand-build lenses.
- **emailSeedSavers** `apps/api/scripts/seed.ts`: For savedByApp seed files; plain seed upserts skip save guards.
- **emailSourceValues** `apps/api/src/lib/email`: provide real Tag and Segment picker options for an email lens
- **emailVersioning** `apps/api/src/hooks/emailVersioning`: stamp component versions and backprop fresh snapshots to ancestors on component changes
- **inScope** `Email docs § Deliver gate ①`: Scope gate; preference opt-outs use canDeliver.
- **isEmailContentError** `Email docs § Deliver`: Content errors fail without retry; other pre-claim errors throw so the job retries.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a chain of instanceof checks against EmailRenderError, MjmlValidationError, TokenValidationError and friends to decide retry vs fail (catalog: isEmailContentError (use instead of chaining instanceof checks))
- **lensFor** `apps/api/src/lib/email/sender.ts`: get the scalar-column lens for a sender type
- **lensScopeSurface** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > The email lens`: scope the builder surface to a loop position
- **mapRefs** `packages/email/src/render/extractRefs.ts`: extract component slugs referenced in MJML
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a regex over {{#component:slug}} to pull component slugs or bodies out of MJML (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Component System › Extraction (mapRefs))
- **omitForeignKeys** `packages/db/lens`: Rule-tracked lenses; redactLens for stripping sensitive fields instead.
- **onIssue** `apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts`: platform (default) for stable unbranded send; fail to wait for a fix via retries/DLQ; degrade to send with empty blocks.
- **parseBlocks / decompose** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Email > Implementation Status`: split authored MJML into reusable component blocks
- **preventHardDelete** `packages/db`: block client hard deletes of a model
- **prune** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Communications`: drop hidden list elements and null hidden relations or root per lens picks
- **resolveFromAddress** `apps/api/src/lib/email/sender.ts`: Full sender variables: resolveSender instead.
- **resolveSender** `apps/api/src/lib/email/sender.ts`: From-address only: resolveFromAddress instead.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* reading organization.name / a from-address off the template row to decide who an email is sent as (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Sender (identity is separate from branding))
- **resolveVariants** `packages/email/src/render/resolveVariants.ts`: match an existing component variant or create a new one
- **RULE_REFERENCEABLE_MODELS** `packages/db`: Registry is the source of truth; never hardcode referenceable models per surface.
- **RuleErrorSink** `@template/email/render`: collect render issues for degraded rules, failed filters and empty tokens
- **RuleReference** `packages/db/prisma/schema/ruleReference.prisma`: Written by the sync and stamped by ruleReference:target; never write ad hoc.
- **ruleReference:target** `packages/db (referenced-side hook)`: stamp rule reference edges when a referenced target row changes
- **RuleReferenceError** `packages/db`: signal a refused dynamic, missing, deleted or inadmissible rule reference
- **ruleReferenceIssues** `packages/db`: derive missing and deleted reference issues from edge rows alone
- **ruleReferences** `packages/db ruleReferences`: raw rules; for email MJML/subject content use contentRuleReferences instead
- **ruleVocabularyIssues** `@template/shared/rules`: render time; save time uses assertValidConditions
- **sendEmail** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Email > Implementation Status`: application sends; call client.send directly only below the job pipeline
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* calling createResendClient(...).send / defaultEmailClient().send from business logic, or enqueuing sendEmail by hand with a recipient list, instead of emitting an app event with an EmailHandoff (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Send Pipeline (event-driven, two BullMQ jobs, never a direct client call; no caller-supplied recipients))
- **SenderType** `apps/api/src/lib/email/sender.ts`: discriminate which identity an email is sent as
- **slotRowsLens** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Planner (sendEmail)`: batch-fetch recipients through recipient lens with targeting where, pruned
- **sourceQueryValues** `json-rules / apps/api`: For candidate values; sourceQueryWhere for where filters. Both refuse bridged sources without farSide.
- **sourceQueryWhere** `json-rules / apps/api`: For filters rather than value lists; sourceQueryValues otherwise.
- **substitute** `apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts`: Over onIssue 'platform' when a specific alternate template should go out; substitutes cannot chain.
- **substituteVariables** `@template/email/render`: Use via interpolate.
- **syncRuleReferenceEdges** `packages/db`: any rule-bearing column; email content goes through syncRuleReferences front
- **System tokens** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Sender`: Sender-specific values: {{sender.*}} instead.
- **targetedBySender** `apps/api/src/lib/email/emailLensFor.ts`: Rule-driven sends from Organization/Space senders; registry sends target the entity's own recipient instead.
- **validateRuleInLens** `@template/shared/rules`: check the current lens still admits a stored rule
- **withoutDegradedSegments** `Email docs § Deliver`: drop segments with degraded rules from the live set before rule evaluation
- **withRule** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > The email lens`: gate template content on a rule at render
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* evaluating a stored rule without first asking whether its bindings are supplied, the lens still admits it and the rows it names are live (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Rule References (withRule is the one fork a stored rule is evaluated through anywhere))
- **Bridged sources need farSide** `sourceQueryValues / sourceQueryWhere`: Whenever a source crosses a bridge.
- **Component MJML skips full-document validation** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Save Pipeline`: Saving component fragments.
- **Component refs stay slug-keyed** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md`: componentRefs resolve by slug via owner cascade, never persisted ids in edge table.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* persisting EmailComponent ids on the template or in an edge table instead of slug-keyed componentRefs (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Rule References (component references stay slug-keyed and do not ride this table))
- **Degraded rules change nothing** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md withRule`: A degraded rule never matches nor touches existing state and must report why.
- **Do not reshape paginated responses with lens projection** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Communications`: Routes with filterLens and paginated responses; projection where clauses would drop rows.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* Running a lens projection (projectRows, prune) over an already paginated page to shape the response instead of the route's responseSchema. (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § The email lens (filterLens vs responseSchema))
- **Dynamic references refused at save** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md`: Save must refuse rules whose referenced rows cannot be determined.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* Saving a rule whose id source is a bind, a path, contains or between and recording no edge for it, instead of refusing it at save. (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Rule References (dynamicRuleReferences))
- **Email lens owner per site** `apps/api/src/lib/email/emailLensFor.ts`: When choosing which owner scopes an email lens.
- **email paths and rules go through the lens** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > The email lens`: Any token, path or rule in an email template.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* Calling check(rule, variables) on a raw email rule at send, or resolving template token paths against raw variables, without the email lens. (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § The email lens ("settle never checks a raw rule"))
- **Event-anchored idempotency keys** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md`: Every email plan/deliver step; intentional resends emit a distinct event.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an idempotency key built from a timestamp or random id, or mutated to force a resend (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Deliver (intentional resends are distinct events, never key mutation))
- **Event-driven email send** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Send Pipeline`: Any outbound email from business logic.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an email sent inline in a route or service handler through a provider client (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Send Pipeline)
- **Fallback renders through primary lens** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#render-issues`: Whenever platform fallback or substitute renders.
- **Generic reference include** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md`: Consumers include sourceRuleReferences and never grow per-model includes.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* Growing a per-model include (tag, space, segment) to judge a rule's references instead of include: { sourceRuleReferences: true } read by ruleReferenceIssues. (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Rule References (staleness lives on the edge))
- **Identity separate from branding** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Sender`: Choosing sender vs template for an email.
- **List-Unsubscribe headers on non-system email** `Email docs § Deliver step 6`: All non-system sends.
- **Memberships are the sender's** `apps/api/src/lib/email/emailLensFor.ts`: Every email send exposing membership rows.
- **Merge scope into first narrowing** `apps/api/src/lib/email/emailLensFor.ts (clampLens)`: When clamps read columns the slot hides (json-rules 3.4 later-layer limits).
- **Never store degradation** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md`: Rule degradation is never stored; staleness lives on edges as two signals.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* A `stale` / `degraded` / `broken` column on the rule-bearing row, set when a referenced row is deleted. (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Rule References ("Nothing about degradation is stored"))
- **No addresses on the queue** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Planner (sendEmail)`: Any per-recipient delivery job.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a job payload carrying the recipient's email address or hydrated user row instead of the recipient id plus the bound targeting where (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Planner (sendEmail) step 2)
- **No caller-supplied recipients** `SendEmailPayload`: Any email send payload.
- **Only queued email logs are open** `lib/email/deliverEmailMessage.ts`: Every email delivery, retry, duplicate job or re-dispatch.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a retry or resend path that reopens a sending/failed row or sends without the queued → sending compare-and-set claim (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Deliver (only a queued row is open; every terminal write is CAS-guarded))
- **opaque data loop restriction** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > The email lens`: Any rule inside {{#each}} over opaque data.
- **Pre-claim errors retry, content errors fail** `lib/email/deliverEmailMessage.ts`: Any failure before the queued→sending claim.
- **Provider send idempotency and retry policy** `lib/email/deliverEmailMessage.ts`: Every provider email send; outcome failures are recorded, not thrown.
- **Referenceable models from registry** `packages/db PolymorphismRegistry.RuleReference`: Making a new model rule-referenceable.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* A surface-local list of which models a rule may reference instead of a PolymorphismRegistry.RuleReference entry (RULE_REFERENCEABLE_MODELS) plus an FK column. (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Rule References ("Which models are referenceable is the registry's answer"))
- **Render degrades silently, save validates** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Interpolate (per recipient)`: All email rendering; render issues indicate drift since save.
- **Render issue behaviour in registry** `apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts`: Any template needing non-default render-issue behaviour.
- **Render issue policy** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md > Email > Implementation Status`: when templates reference variables or rules
- **Rendering enforces lens projection** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Communications`: Any email render using a lens-scoped variable set.

- **Seed through api seed script** `apps/api/scripts/seed.ts`: Any seed including email templates/components; packages/db seed refuses savedByApp files.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* inserting seed rows with a one-off script or `db.x.createMany` outside the seed runner, skipping hooks and save guards (packages/db seed refuses savedByApp files) (apps/api/scripts/seed.ts)

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/database-models -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Database Models (in "Communications")

##### Database Models

###### EmailTemplate

MJML templates with ownership and componentRefs.

```prisma
model EmailTemplate {
  id               String
  name             String              // "OTP Verification"
  slug             String              // "otp"
  locale           String              // "en"
  kind             CommunicationKind   // system|platform|activity|marketing
  subject          String              // "Your code: {{data.code}}"
  mjml             String              // Full MJML with component refs
  componentRefs    String[]            // Pre-computed slugs

  // Ownership (false polymorphism)
  ownerModel       EmailOwnerModel     // default|admin|Organization|Space
  organizationId   String?
  spaceId          String?
  inheritToSpaces  Boolean             // Allow Space to use Org template
}
```

###### EmailComponent

Reusable MJML blocks (headers, footers, buttons).

```prisma
model EmailComponent {
  id               String
  slug             String              // "default-header"
  mjml             String              // MJML fragment
  locale           String
  componentRefs    String[]            // Nested component slugs

  // Same ownership pattern as EmailTemplate
  ownerModel       EmailOwnerModel
  organizationId   String?
  spaceId          String?
  inheritToSpaces  Boolean
}
```

###### CommunicationLog

Per-recipient delivery ledger — one row per recipient per send (grouped by `sendKey`) — and the
deduplicated send intent (`idempotencyKey @unique`). It stores the settled MJML, render variables
(including the hydrated recipient projection), render issues, and template/component audit references.
It does not store the final provider HTML. Sender is false-polymorphic; `kind`/`emailTemplateId`
are filled when delivery resolves the template.

```prisma
model CommunicationLog {
  id                   String
  sendKey              String                // groups a send's recipients (= planner job id)
  channel              CommunicationChannel  // email|sms|push|inApp
  kind                 CommunicationKind?    // filled at deliver
  status               CommunicationStatus   // queued→sending→sent | failed | suppressed | undeliverable
  emailTemplateId      String?               // resolved template (onDelete: SetNull)

  senderType           SenderType            // false polymorphism (platform/admin carry no FK)
  senderUserId         String?
  senderOrganizationId String?
  senderSpaceId        String?

  recipientUserId      String?
  recipientContactId   String?
  address              String

  idempotencyKey       String                // @unique — the fence
  providerMessageId    String?
  error                String?
  reasonCode           CommunicationReasonCode?  // why a failed row failed — see Deliver
  sentAt               DateTime?
}
```

###### Enums

```prisma
enum CommunicationKind {
  system        // OTP, password reset, security — always delivered, un-mute-able
  platform      // product news, announcements — opt-out
  activity      // something happened involving you — opt-out
  marketing     // promo — opt-in only
}

enum CommunicationChannel { email  sms  push  inApp }

enum CommunicationStatus {
  queued  sending  sent  failed  suppressed  undeliverable
}

enum EmailOwnerModel {
  default       // Base templates - read: all, write: super admin
  admin         // Platform internal - super admin only
  Organization  // Tenant-branded
  Space         // Space-specific overrides
}

```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/component-system -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Component System (in "Communications")

##### Component System

###### Syntax

```mjml
{{#component:header}}
  <mj-section>
    {{#component:logo}}
      <mj-image src="logo.png" />
    {{/component:logo}}
  </mj-section>
{{/component:header}}
```

Pattern: `{{#component:slug}}...{{/component:slug}}`

###### Extraction (mapRefs)

```typescript
import { mapRefs } from '@template/email/render';

const result = mapRefs(mjmlString);
// result.map - { slug: [{ mjml, refs }] }
// result.mjml - Tagged output with :N indices
// result.refs - Top-level refs
```

Handles:
- Nested components (depth N)
- Variant deduplication (same MJML = same component)
- Variant indexing (`:0`, `:1` for different content)

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/variable-interpolation -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Variable Interpolation (in "Communications")

##### Variable Interpolation

Three prefixes for variable substitution:

| Prefix | Source | Example |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `sender` | Platform or org info | `{{sender.name}}` |
| `recipient` | Recipient user | `{{recipient.email}}` |
| `data` | Explicit from send call | `{{data.code}}` |

```typescript
import { interpolate } from '@template/email/render';

const html = interpolate(template, {
  sender: { name: 'Acme Corp' },
  recipient: { email: 'user@example.com', firstName: 'John' },
  data: { code: '123456' },
});
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/the-email-lens -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › The email lens (in "Communications")

##### The email lens

An email renders against four scope roots — `sender`, `recipient`, `data`, `system` — and the
email lens is **four lenses, one per root** (`EmailLens`, `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts`):
a User narrowing for the recipient, the sender model's narrowing, a model or declared-field lens
for `data` (or the opaque bag, addressable at any depth as beneath-Json), and a declared lens over
the system tokens. No bridges between them; a comparison across two roots is a `path` into the
other lens. Everything a template does with a path or a rule goes through it:

- **Tokens and paths** — `walkEmailLensPath` / `emailTokenPathKind` walk the *narrowing* (a slot
  that drops a relation drops its tokens), at save (`validateTokens`), for component expectations
  and in preflight.
- **Rules** — `emailRuleViolations` is the vocabulary (save and `withRule` at render),
  `emailRuleReferences` the rows a rule names, and `applyEmailLens` + `check` the evaluation:
  settle never checks a raw rule, so a lens `where` decides at send what it decides at save. A
  rule inside `{{#each}}` is the array rule it always was (`scopedRule`): one `any` per enclosing
  loop, binding leaves element-relative, root leaves climbing with `$$`; vocabulary, references
  and evaluation all read that one form, and evaluation runs slot-relative against the iterated
  collection pinned to the element in scope (`narrowToElements`, `evaluateScopedRule`). A loop over
  the opaque `data` bag has no lens to fold, so a rule inside it may not read a lens-backed root at
  all (`opaqueLoopIssue`): refused at save (`validateConditions`) and at render. Template save and
  dependent re-validation check the *composed* template, so a cascade-resolved component is judged
  against the embedding template's lens.
- **The builder** — `emailSurface` composes the four exposed surfaces under a presentation root
  `Email` for the rule surface route: the maps each slot's projection shows, plus a narrowing whose
  `root.relations` turns each slot on and, beneath it, the slot's own shown tree (columns kept per
  path), so the builder gates against the narrowed lens (`composeNarrowed(source)`) and walks loops
  with `lensScopeSurface(lens, { at })`. Fetched options are keyed at the slot's path under `Email`
  (`emailSurfaceSourceValues`). `emailRuleDecoration` derives one facet per lens present.

**The lens is the row owner's.** `emailLensFor(slug, owner)` (`apps/api/src/lib/email/emailLensFor.ts`)
builds the slug's declared lens (the registry entry's sender and data lenses, the User recipient
over `DEFAULT_RECIPIENT_NARROWING`, a sender slot from the actual sender when no entry declares
one; every prisma slot foreign-key-free and redacted) and narrows it by the slots stored on the
row — or on the slug's default-tier row when the row carries none. A stored slot is a **later
layer**: it shows exactly what it names and can never turn on what the declared surface does not
(a stored recipient lens naming `sessions` or `accounts` is refused). The lens is scoped to the
owner of the row being saved, edited or rendered (`scopeEmailLens`): tags are platform-owned or the
owner's, segments are the owner's (via `recipient.providerRefs.segmentMembers.segment`), platform
tiers see platform tags and no segments; the link rows are bound the same way — a tag attachment or
segment membership by its far side, a customer ref by its provider.
`OrganizationUser`/`SpaceUser` rows scope to the person, like the cascade they sit on. The scope
is merged into each slot's **first** narrowing (json-rules `clampLens`): json-rules 3.4 lets a later layer's
clamp read only what its parent shows, and these clamps read columns the slot hides.
**Memberships are the sender's.** At send, `emailLensFor(slug, owner, stored, sender)` also clamps
`OrganizationUser` / `SpaceUser` rows to the sending owner's tree (`senderLensOwner`): an
Organization, OrganizationUser, Space or SpaceUser sender to its organization (the organization and
all its spaces, a space's parent included); a User sender to none; a platform or admin send is
unrestricted. Nothing outside that organization ever shows. The clamp bounds; the lens chooses what
shows inside it. By default (`defaultRecipientNarrowing`) a sender sees its own level only: an
Organization its organization memberships, a Space its own space's memberships, a User none, a
platform or admin both. A stored recipient lens that turns on `organizationUsers` or `spaceUsers`
widens it, still within the organization. Targeting follows the same bound: a `messageUser` rule
from an Organization- or Space-level sender reaches only people holding a membership the recipient
lens shows (`targetedBySender`), so a space reaches its own members by default and its organization's
when its lens widens. Registry sends target the entity's own recipient (an invite's target need not
be a member yet). Without a sender (save, preview, rule surface) the template owner stands in. The owner
is decided per site: save takes it from the input, the rule surface and preflight from the body
(default: platform), and settle from `composeTemplate`'s `owner` — the row that won the cascade,
so an Organization row rendered for a Space sender sees the organization's tags. No inheritance up
the tree for now. The picker gets real options for Tag and Segment (`emailSourceValues`, the lens's
`toSourceQueries` run through Prisma by `sourceQueryValues`, keyed onto the `email` surface map by
`emailSurfaceSourceValues`). A source across a bridge returns candidates (`recheck`):
`sourceQueryValues` / `sourceQueryWhere` re-check them with the far side the caller's `farSide`
loads, and refuse them without it. A referenced model's path source points at its own model source
(`sources: { id: { from: 'mapDefaults' } }`), so it offers every row the owner may name, not only
rows already linked down the path. Organization and Space are scoped on both the model and
its ID source: an Organization owner sees itself and its spaces; a Space owner sees itself
and its organization; a User owner sees neither; platform rows leave these two models unrestricted.
The picker uses those same source queries.

**Rendering enforces the projection too.** `interpolate` calls `narrowVariables` before any
token or rule reads a slot. `prune` applies both picks and each visit's `where`: hidden list
elements are dropped, hidden to-one relations become null, and a hidden root becomes null.
An unfiltered loop cannot expose a foreign tag through a token while the corresponding rule
would refuse it. Token/path traversal delegates to json-rules' `walkLensPath`.

A route's `filterLens` is a different role: it controls accepted filters and sorting, while
`responseSchema` controls the response. Do not use this projection step to reshape an already
paginated response; its `where` clauses can remove rows from the page.

**Deferred (documented, not built):**

- **Template variants and liveness** — `variant`, `live`, tombstone revival and flag-selected
  variants remain the proposal in [COMM-014](../../tickets/COMM-014-template-variants-and-untombstone.md).
  The current schema has neither column and `saveScopedRow` only finds live rows before
  update-or-create; it does not revive a deleted natural key.

- **Subtenancy brand lock** — an `Organization`-level `spaceEmailPolicy:
  free | locked` (+ locked/required component slugs). On `locked`, the cascade
  stops letting a Space override the locked slugs and save/render
  requires/injects them. The component-inheritance mechanism already exists; only
  the lock/enforcement is missing. No settings table exists today; this would land
  on the `Organization` app-fields fence.
- **FF-gated additive lens grants** — entitlement/module ownership stitches extra
  `data` fields into the lens; the base lens stays static + superadmin-authored.
- **Predicate-composited surfaces** — not pursued (no stable contract to validate
  against); content variation stays in conditional blocks.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/cascade-resolution -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Cascade Resolution (in "Communications")

##### Cascade Resolution

Two separate ownership chains, selected by the sender's tier — a user-actor walks the **user** chain, a tenant/shared sender walks the **org** chain. Both end at the shared `default` floor.

| Context (sender tier) | Resolution Order |
|---------|------------------|
| SpaceUser | SpaceUser → OrganizationUser → User → default |
| OrganizationUser | OrganizationUser → User → default |
| User | User → default |
| Space | Space → Org (if `inheritToSpaces`) → default |
| Organization | Org → default |
| admin | admin → default |
| default | default only |

This cascade happens automatically during compose - `composeTemplate` and `composeComponent` handle lookup based on the ownership context.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/render-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Render Pipeline (in "Communications")

##### Render Pipeline

The render pipeline has two phases:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PHASE 1: Compose (once per template)                       │
│  composeTemplate(slug, ctx) → { id, mjml, subject, kind }   │
│     └── expand(mjml, componentRefs, ctx)                    │
│         └── lookupCascade → fetch components → replace refs │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PHASE 2: Interpolate (per recipient)                       │
│  for (recipient of recipients) {                            │
│    interpolate(mjml, { sender, recipient, data })           │
│      └── evaluateConditions ({{#if rule=...}})              │
│      └── substituteVariables ({{sender.*}}, etc.)           │
│  }                                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Phase 1** happens once - fetch template, expand all `{{#component:slug}}` refs.

**Phase 2** happens per recipient - evaluate conditionals and substitute variables.

###### Compose

```typescript
import { composeTemplate, composeComponent } from '@template/email/render';

// Compose a full template
const { mjml, subject, kind } = await composeTemplate('welcome', {
  ownerModel: 'Organization',
  organizationId: org.id,
  locale: 'en',
});

// Compose a single component (for editor preview)
const { mjml } = await composeComponent('header', {
  ownerModel: 'default',
  locale: 'en',
});
```

###### Interpolate (per recipient)

```typescript
import { interpolate } from '@template/email/render';

const recipients = [user1, user2, user3];

for (const recipient of recipients) {
  const html = interpolate(mjml, {
    sender: { name: 'Acme Corp', logo: 'https://...' },
    recipient: { name: recipient.name, email: recipient.email, role: recipient.role },
    data: { code: generateOtp() },
  });

  // Now render MJML to HTML and send
}
```

`interpolate(template, variables, onError?, { locale, liveRefs, lens })` and
`evaluateConditions(template, variables, onError?, liveRefs?)` take an optional
`onError: RuleErrorSink` (`(issue: RenderIssue) => void`, `RenderIssue = { kind:
'rule' | 'token' | 'each', path?, detail }`). Render has one behaviour: a block whose
rule is degraded (`withRule`: a required binding missing, the lens no longer admits
the rule, a row it names is gone) or throws renders nothing; an `{{#each}}` whose
filter throws renders nothing; a token that resolves to nothing, to an object, or to
an unknown root renders **empty** — never the literal `{{…}}`. Every such case is one
issue in the sink. Save is where the lens decides (`validateTokens`,
`validateConditions`), so at render an issue means drift since save, not authoring.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/save-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Save Pipeline (in "Communications")

##### Save Pipeline

Coordinates template + component persistence:

```typescript
import { saveEmailTemplate } from '@template/email/render';

const { template, components } = await saveEmailTemplate(db, {
  slug: 'welcome',
  name: 'Welcome Email',
  subject: 'Welcome, {{recipient.firstName}}!',
  mjml: '<mjml>...</mjml>',
  category: 'system',
  ownerModel: 'Organization',
  organizationId: 'org_123',
  locale: 'en',
});
```

Pipeline steps:
1. Validate MJML syntax + conditional rules in `mjml` and `subject`
   (`assertValidConditions`) — fail fast instead of shipping a render-time time-bomb
2. Extract component refs (`mapRefs`)
3. Lookup existing components via cascade
4. Resolve variants (match or create)
5. Save template + components in transaction (each component re-validates its own
   conditionals at the unit boundary; component MJML is a fragment, so it is not
   run through the full-document MJML validator)

// Both are also re-exported from the package root: '@template/email'

try {

} catch (err) {

}

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/template-versioning-recompose -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Template Versioning & Recompose (in "Communications")

##### Template Versioning & Recompose

"What was sent" stays reconstructable after templates and shared components are edited. Live
`EmailTemplate`/`EmailComponent` rows keep using **slug refs** (late-bound through the cascade — a
Space override can be added or evacuated and existing templates re-resolve live). The **version graph
lives in the audit log**:

- Every edit already writes an immutable `AuditLog` snapshot (`after` = full content). The
  `emailVersioning` hook additionally stamps `AuditLog.componentVersions` — a `{ slug → child snapshot
  audit-log id }` map of the snapshots the row's children currently resolve to. A template snapshot
  points at its component snapshots, recursively: a traversable version tree, each version's content
  stored once and shared by reference when unchanged.
- **Backprop walk** (`apps/api/src/hooks/emailVersioning`): a component change — content edit, or an
  override created/deleted that shifts resolution — spawns fresh snapshots for every ancestor whose
  resolved children moved, stopping a branch where an override shadows the change. Saves run
  **children-before-parent** so a parent snapshot pins children that already exist; the hook registers
  *after* the audit hook so the changed row's snapshot exists when the walk runs.
- **Send pins the version**: `deliverEmail` records the template's current snapshot id on
  `CommunicationLog.emailTemplateAuditLogId`.
- **Recompose** (`recomposeCommunication`, `apps/api/src/lib/email/recompose.ts`): resolves
  `CommunicationLog.emailTemplateAuditLogId` then `recomposeSnapshot` walks `componentVersions`
  recursively, splicing each pinned child snapshot back into its `{{#component:slug}}` block, to rebuild
  the as-sent composition. Version fidelity (template + components as they were), `{{variable.*}}`
  placeholders intact — not the per-recipient interpolated bytes.
- **Seeds**: the `packages/db` seed can't import `registerHooks`, so the canonical seed runs through
  `apps/api/scripts/seed.ts`, which registers all hooks first — seeded system templates get their
  initial snapshots. Email seed files are `savedByApp`: the api seed persists them through
  `emailSeedSavers` (`saveEmailComponents`, the api `saveEmailTemplate`), so a seeded row meets
  the guards its save runs (a template: MJML, conditions, lens tokens, rule references; a component:
  MJML, conditions, rule references) and one that would not validate fails the run. They seed last,
  after the cron jobs. The `packages/db` seed alone refuses them.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#email/rule-references-the-rows-a-rule-names -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Email › Rule References (the rows a rule names) (in "Communications")

##### Rule References (the rows a rule names)

A `{{#if rule=…}}` block can name a row — "recipient is tagged X", "recipient is in space Y". Those
edges are persisted so that "who references X" is an index and a stale rule is never evaluated
(INFRA-030).

- **`RuleReference`** (`packages/db/prisma/schema/ruleReference.prisma`): one row per
  (source row → target row), false-polymorphic on both ends — `sourceModel` + one typed FK per
  rule-bearing model (`sourceEmailTemplateId` / `sourceEmailComponentId` / `sourceSegmentId`), `targetModel` + one typed FK per
  referenceable model (`targetTagId` / `targetOrganizationId` / `targetSpaceId` / `targetSegmentId`), both axes in `PolymorphismRegistry`.
  Real relations on both ends: the source side cascades, the target side is left to `SET NULL` on a
  purge. Edges are written by the sync (create, delete, restamp) and stamped by `ruleReference:target`.
- **Which models are referenceable is the registry's answer, not any surface's.**
  `RULE_REFERENCEABLE_MODELS` (`packages/db`) is the `targetModel` axis of
  `PolymorphismRegistry.RuleReference`; the referenced-side hook registers on it.
- **A rule-tracked lens has one spelling per reference: the row's `id`, never an FK column.**
  `omitForeignKeys(lens)` (`packages/db/lens`, the same shape as `redactLens`) omits every FK
  column `prismaMap` knows from every model, wherever it appears; each rule-tracked lens wraps
  itself in it and declares its own id sources. Each model-rooted lens of the email lens
  (`emailLens`, `packages/email/src/rules/emailLens.ts`) wraps in `omitForeignKeys` and declares
  `sources: { id: { label: 'name' } }` as a `mapDefaults` entry for each of
  `RULE_REFERENCEABLE_MODELS`, so the id answers on every path to the model. The default
  recipient lens reaches `tagAttachments.tag`, `spaceUsers.space`, `organizationUsers.organization`
  and `providerRefs.segmentMembers.segment` (`id`, `name`); a relation the lens does not declare
  is refused at save. The api's `emailLensFor(slug, owner)` builds the owner-scoped lens; the
  builder gets `emailSurface` of it (which strips clamps and sources), while save and settle keep the lens
  itself (`defaultEmailLens` when none is threaded) — extraction never runs on the exposed
  surface. Adding a referenceable model = a registry entry + an FK column (the hook and email's
  sources derive); a surface that reaches it declares its own labeled id source.
- **Extraction is the lens's** (`ruleReferences(lens, rule)`, `packages/db`): `describeRuleSources`
  (json-rules ≥ 3.0) reports the values a rule names at each source, and a source on a model's
  id field is a row reference. Nested and dotted spellings are one path; a `path`/`bind` leaf at a
  source — or an operator that describes the row without naming it (`contains`, `between`) — is
  `dynamic`: no save can check which rows it names, so save refuses it (`dynamicRuleReferences`;
  email throws `RuleReferenceError`, a segment's conditions fail validation). When save is handed a lens (the api
  always is), its condition gate (`assertValidConditions`) refuses any rule path the lens does not
  resolve — an FK spelling or typo path is a 422, never a silently unregistered rule; `withRule`
  asks the same question at render through `ruleVocabularyIssues`. With no lens there is nothing
  to decide and only extraction runs.
- **Edges are written by the save path, not a hook.** The writer is
  `syncRuleReferenceEdges(owner, references, gate)` in `packages/db` — set-diff (survivors
  keep their row), a newly added missing or soft-deleted target refused as a delta (a pre-existing
  dead reference stays editable), referenced rows locked with `db.findForUpdate` while the gate
  reads them, and every kept edge restamped against its target. With `gate: { lenses }` (each
  lens's `toSourceQueries`), a newly added reference the
  source's composed `where` does not admit is refused too (`admitRuleReferences`): that is how
  an Organization template cannot name another organization's tag or segment. Throws
  `RuleReferenceError`. Adding a rule-bearing column = a `syncRuleReferenceEdges`
  call from its save path. Email's `syncRuleReferences(source, contents, lens, mode)` is the
  content-shaped front: it collects the rules out of MJML and subject (`contentRuleReferences`)
  and hands the references down. `saveEmailTemplate` calls it inside
  its transaction for the template and each saved component; it is the only writer of
  `mjml`/`subject`, so nothing bypasses it.
- **Staleness lives on the edge, as two signals rather than a computed flag.** A soft delete of a
  referenced row is copied onto every edge naming it by `ruleReference:target` (one
  `updateManyAndReturn`, matched on `(targetModel, targetId)`, cleared on undelete); a
  purge `SET NULL`s the typed FK and leaves `targetId` naming the row that went. The referenced
  axis therefore carries true polymorphism beside the false — the FK is the relation and may go
  null, `targetId` is the name and never changes, and the sync writes both from one value.
  `ruleReferenceIssues(edges)` reads both from the edge rows alone, so consumers
  write `include: { sourceRuleReferences: true }` and never grow that include as models become
  referenceable. At render, `composeTemplate` reads the template's edges plus those of the
  components the cascade resolved into one live set, and every branch goes through **`withRule`**
  (`@template/shared/rules`) — the one fork a stored rule is evaluated through anywhere.
- **`withRule(health, { degraded, sound })`** asks, at evaluation and against the current lens,
  whether the rule can be evaluated correctly — two questions: every binding it requires is
  supplied (`bindOptional` marks the ones that may be left out and resolve to null), and it is
  still valid — the lens admits it (`validateRuleInLens`, so a lens change after save degrades
  the rule instead of silently narrowing it) and every row it names is in the live set the caller
  confirmed (absent set = nothing confirmed = every reference missing). Degraded means "do nothing
  new, say why": in email that is a rule issue, never a match, and the registry entry's `render`
  spec decides the send; existing state is never touched by a degraded rule. Sound runs
  the caller's evaluator. Extraction (`ruleReferences`) lives in `packages/db` with the registry
  that knows which sources are ids; the live set comes from the caller's own read, locked when the
  sound arm decides money. Nothing about degradation is stored. Client hard deletes stay prevented
  (`preventHardDelete`).
- Component references (`componentRefs`) stay slug-keyed and do **not** ride this table: they
  resolve through the owner cascade at read time, so an id persisted at save would be wrong the
  moment an override appears.

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#email-system -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Email System (in "Template Features")

#### Email System

- ✅ **Templates and Components** — Stored MJML, subjects, locales, reusable nested components, audit-backed versions and owner-tier cascade. Ownership supports default/admin, User, Organization, Space, OrganizationUser and SpaceUser tiers.
- ✅ **Planner and Delivery** — App-event handoffs select a registry template plus bindings. `sendEmail` resolves sender and recipients, records per-recipient `CommunicationLog` intent and enqueues `deliverEmail`; delivery settles, renders, sends and records the outcome.
- ✅ **Preferences and Verification** — Communication kind, contact acceptance and cached address deliverability participate in delivery. System messages bypass preference opt-out; other kinds must be accepted by the contact.
- ✅ **Owner-Scoped Email Lenses** — Separate sender, recipient, data and system lenses govern tokens, rules, loops, picker options and runtime projection. Recipient data can include scoped tags and segment memberships; foreign data is filtered before interpolation.
- ✅ **Rule References and Degradation** — Save paths maintain `RuleReference` edges; stale or transitively degraded segment references affect rule health. Preflight and render use the same lens vocabulary and reference admission.
- ✅ **Authoring API** — Template/component save, rule-surface and preflight endpoints exist. The complete visual authoring experience remains work in progress.
- 🟣 **Variants and Liveness** — `variant`/`live`, tombstone revival and flag-selected template variants are specified in COMM-014 but are not in the current implementation.

[Learn more: COMMUNICATIONS.md](docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md)
